## Q1
Which of the following statements explains the concepts of inclusive teaching ?

## Q1 - Options
(A) Teacher facilitates the learning of the gifted students.
(B) Teacher facilitates the learning of the weak students.
(C) Teacher takes support of parents of the students to make them learn.
(D) Teacher makes the students of different backgounds to learn together in the same class.

## Q1 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Teaching Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q1

Inclusive teaching is grounded in bringing learners from diverse socio-economic, linguistic, cultural, and cognitive backgrounds together in an equitable, shared classroom environment.

- **A. Teacher facilitates the learning of the gifted students.** — focuses exclusively on high achievers rather than all students.
- **B. Teacher facilitates the learning of the weak students.** — addresses remedial learning in isolation rather than full classroom integration.
- **C. Teacher takes support of parents of the students to make them learn.** — describes parental engagement rather than inclusive pedagogical design.
- **D. Teacher makes the students of different backgounds to learn together in the same class.** — correct. Captures the core philosophy of educating heterogeneous student groups collaboratively in one common space.

## Q2
To organize discussion method in teaching effectively, which of the following conditions should be met ?

(1) Topic be easy<br>
(2) Topic be declared in advance<br>
(3) Topic of common interest<br>
(4) Availability of more than one teacher<br>
(5) Language facility of participate

Select appropriate answer from the options given below:

## Q2 - Options
(A) (2), (3) and (5)
(B) (1), (2) and (3)
(C) (1), (2) and (5)
(D) (3), (4) and (5)

## Q2 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Teaching Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q2

An effective classroom discussion relies on preparation, shared learner motivation, and communication competence.

- **(2) Topic declared in advance** allows learners time to gather facts, read background literature, and formulate well-reasoned arguments.
- **(3) Topic of common interest** ensures active, self-motivated learner involvement across the entire group.
- **(5) Language facility of participants** ensures students possess the expressive competence required to articulate viewpoints clearly.
- **(1) Topic be easy** is counterproductive because discussions are specifically meant to explore nuanced, complex problems.
- **(4) Availability of more than one teacher** is unnecessary for standard classroom discussions, which are routinely led by a single facilitator.

## Q3
Which of the following is a plagiarism website ?

## Q3 - Options
(A) http://go.turnitin.com
(B) http://www.researchgate.com
(C) http://www.editorial.elsevier.com
(D) http://www.grammarly.com

## Q3 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q3

Turnitin is a dedicated commercial plagiarism detection and text-similarity matching service widely adopted by universities to verify academic originality.

- **A. http://go.turnitin.com** — correct. Checks submitted manuscripts against billions of web pages and institutional repositories for unoriginal text.
- **B. http://www.researchgate.com** — an academic networking platform for researchers to share papers and collaborate.
- **C. http://www.editorial.elsevier.com** — a peer-review and manuscript management platform for Elsevier academic journals.
- **D. http://www.grammarly.com** — primarily an automated writing assistant focused on grammar, clarity, and tone.

## Q4
Which among the following best describes the Emotional Intelligence of learners ?

(1) Understand the emotion of other people and your own.<br>
(2) Express oneself very strongly.<br>
(3) Being rational in thinking.<br>
(4) Adjusting one’s emotion as per situation.<br>
(5) Being creative and open to criticism.<br>
(6) Accepting other people as they are.

Choose your answer from the options given below:

## Q4 - Options
(A) (1), (4) and (6)
(B) (4), (5) and (6)
(C) (1), (2) and (3)
(D) (2), (3) and (4)

## Q4 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Teaching Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q4

Emotional intelligence entails recognizing emotional states in oneself and others, regulating emotions constructively, and maintaining empathetic interpersonal relationships.

- **(1) Understand the emotion of other people and your own** represents self-awareness and empathy, the core foundation of emotional intelligence.
- **(4) Adjusting one’s emotion as per situation** represents self-regulation and emotional adaptability.
- **(6) Accepting other people as they are** represents empathetic social awareness and non-judgmental relationship management.
- **(2) Express oneself very strongly** reflects emotional impulsivity or aggressive reactivity rather than emotional regulation.
- **(3) Being rational in thinking** relates to purely cognitive intelligence (IQ) rather than emotional domain processing.

## Q5
In which of the following research studies interpretation and meaning get more attention than formulation of generalisations?

(i) Historical studies<br>
(ii) Survey studies<br>
(iii) Philosophical studies<br>
(iv) Ethnographic studies<br>
(v) Hypothetico – deductive studies<br>
(vi) Ex-post facto studies

Choose your answer from the options given below:

## Q5 - Options
(A) (i), (ii) and (iii)
(B) (iv), (v) and (vi)
(C) (ii), (iv) and (v)
(D) (i), (iii) and (iv)

## Q5 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q5

Qualitative paradigms emphasize interpretive understanding, contextual depth, and subjective meaning rather than statistical generalization across populations.

- **(i) Historical studies** interpret documentary evidence and reconstruct contextual meaning of past human experiences.
- **(iii) Philosophical studies** analyze concepts, epistemological frameworks, and normative meanings through philosophical hermeneutics.
- **(iv) Ethnographic studies** engage in holistic immersion to decode cultural meanings from participants’ perspectives.

By contrast, survey studies (ii), hypothetico-deductive studies (v), and ex-post facto research (vi) follow quantitative, positivist methodologies aimed at statistical generalization and hypothesis testing.

## Q6
Bibliography given in a research report

## Q6 - Options
(A) Helps those interested in further research.
(B) Shows the vast knowledge of the researcher.
(C) Makes the report authentic.
(D) Is an optional part of the report.

## Q6 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q6

A bibliography documents all works consulted or relevant to the subject, enabling subsequent researchers to locate primary and secondary sources to advance further inquiry.

- **A. Helps those interested in further research.** — correct. Provides complete bibliographic metadata so readers can retrieve and build upon the literature.
- **B. Shows the vast knowledge of the researcher.** — misinterprets an academic citation standard as an exercise in personal vanity.
- **C. Makes the report authentic.** — while accurate citations enhance credibility, methodology and verified empirical evidence determine authenticity.
- **D. Is an optional part of the report.** — standard scholarly reports mandate full bibliographic references to avoid plagiarism.

## Q7
The research design is specifically related to which of the following features in research ?

(i) Sample selection<br>
(ii) Formulation of a plan<br>
(iii) Deciding about the tool for data collection<br>
(iv) Hypothesis making<br>
(v) Choice of a field of inquiry

Select your answer from the options given below:

## Q7 - Options
(A) (ii), (iii) and (iv)
(B) (i), (ii) and (iii)
(C) (ii), (iv) and (v)
(D) (iii), (iv) and (v)

## Q7 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q7

A research design is the comprehensive operational blueprint that guides the collection and analysis of data.

- **(i) Sample selection** constitutes the sampling design, establishing sampling technique, frame, and sample size.
- **(ii) Formulation of a plan** provides the overarching operational framework for executing the investigation.
- **(iii) Deciding about the tool for data collection** specifies the measurement instruments, questionnaires, or observational protocols.

By contrast, choosing a field of inquiry (v) and formulating hypotheses (iv) belong to the preliminary conceptual stage that precedes the development of the operational research design.

## Q8
Who developed the theory of ‘Multiple Intelligence’ ?

## Q8 - Options
(A) Alfred Binet
(B) L. Thurstone
(C) Charles Spearman
(D) Howard Gardner

## Q8 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Teaching Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q8

Howard Gardner formulated the Theory of Multiple Intelligences in his 1983 book Frames of Mind, proposing eight distinct modalities of human competence.

- **A. Alfred Binet** — developed the first practical intelligence scale (Binet-Simon test) to measure general mental ability.
- **B. L. Thurstone** — proposed the theory of Primary Mental Abilities, focusing on seven independent factors.
- **C. Charles Spearman** — introduced the two-factor theory of intelligence comprising general factor (g) and specific factors (s).
- **D. Howard Gardner** — correct. Identified linguistic, logical-mathematical, spatial, bodily-kinesthetic, musical, interpersonal, intrapersonal, and naturalistic intelligences.

## Q9
Through which research method, the manipulation of an independent variable and its effect on dependent variable is examined with reference to a hypothesis under controlled conditions ?

## Q9 - Options
(A) Ex-post facto research
(B) Descriptive research
(C) Case study research
(D) Experimental research

## Q9 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q9

Experimental research is defined by active manipulation of independent variables, observation of dependent variables, and rigorous control over extraneous variables.

- **A. Ex-post facto research** — examines phenomena after events have occurred, where the investigator cannot manipulate independent variables.
- **B. Descriptive research** — observes and records conditions as they exist without variable manipulation.
- **C. Case study research** — conducts an in-depth qualitative examination of an individual, group, or institution in a natural setting.
- **D. Experimental research** — correct. Employs direct manipulation under controlled laboratory or field conditions to test cause-and-effect hypotheses.

## Q10
From the list of the effective teaching behaviours, identify those which are called key behaviours.

(i) Direct, audible and oral delivery to all students.<br>
(ii) Encouraging students to elaborate on an answer.<br>
(iii) Warm and nurturing relationships with learners.<br>
(iv) Varying modes of presentation.<br>
(v) Preventing misbehaviour with a minimum of class disruption.<br>
(vi) Organising what is to come and summarising what has gone before.

Select your answer from the options given below:

## Q10 - Options
(A) (i), (iv) and (v)
(B) (i), (ii) and (iii)
(C) (ii), (iii) and (iv)
(D) (iv), (v) and (vi)

## Q10 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Teaching Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q10

In Gary Borich’s observational model of classroom effectiveness, teaching behaviours are categorized into five key behaviours and five helping behaviours.

The five key behaviours are:

1. Lesson Clarity — direct, audible delivery to all students (i)
2. Instructional Variety — varying modes of presentation, questions, and learning materials (iv)
3. Teacher Task Orientation — managing the classroom to minimize disruptive misbehaviour (v)
4. Engagement in the Learning Process
5. Student Success Rate

Items (ii), (iii), and (vi) represent helping behaviours:

- (ii) Encouraging elaboration represents probing.
- (iii) Warm, nurturing relationships represents teacher affect.
- (vi) Organising and summarising represents lesson structuring.

## Q11
What actually may be concluded from the passage ?

Michaelangelo is famous for having successfully interpreted the human body. His great achievement is that of the painting of David whose hands reach out as a sign of human capability and potential. It is assumed that the time he lived was ripe for exchange of knowledge, development in science and matured enough to advance the horizon of investigation in all fields. Renaissance humanism stressed on a serious rethink on the nature of art that focussed on accurate details. In painting and sculpture, artists focussed on not so casual but verifiable and minute details. Michaelangelo’s paintings are no exception to it. In a study published in the journal of the Royal Society of medicine, a group of surgeons are of the opinion that the great master was “afflicted by an illness involving his joints”. They have used his portraits as evidence to argue their view. During his life, he complained of what he felt to be ‘gout’. Later he complained of his sore and stiff hands which the doctors would find to be natural for someone who was engaged in handmade art. The doctors found corroboration of those claims in portraits of the artists that show a hanging left hand with both degenerative and non-degenerative changes. They attribute the pain not just to arthritis, but to the stress of hammering and chiseling and note that though the master was seen hammering days before his death at an old age, he did not write or sign his own letters before his death. In recent times there have been attempts to diagnose famous artists with diseases that were not known during their time. This practice has raised many questions, especially on the issue of ethics in research. It is also inferred from authentic analysis that Michaelangelo persisted in his work until his last days. This theory would emphasize that his artistic subject defied his physical infirmities.

## Q11 - Options
(A) Physical infirmities do dissuade people with capabilities from excelling.
(B) Excellence in any form triumphs over extraneous factors including physical ailments.
(C) Michaelangelo’s gout and other ailments lessened his efficiency.
(D) The diseases Michaelangelo faced were due to constant hammering.

## Q11 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Comprehension
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q11

The passage concludes by noting that Michelangelo persisted in producing monumental art until his final days, emphasizing that his artistic vision triumphed over physical deterioration.

- **A. Physical infirmities do dissuade people with capabilities from excelling.** — directly contradicted by the passage, which shows Michelangelo persevered despite severe pain.
- **B. Excellence in any form triumphs over extraneous factors including physical ailments.** — correct. Captures the central conclusion that artistic dedication defied bodily infirmity.
- **C. Michaelangelo’s gout and other ailments lessened his efficiency.** — contradicted by the passage noting he hammered and worked days before his death at an advanced age.
- **D. The diseases Michaelangelo faced were due to constant hammering.** — the doctors attributed the pain to arthritis combined with hammering stress, not as the sole cause of disease.

## Q16
The proposition ‘No historians are non-mathematician’ is equivalent to which of the following proposition ?

## Q16 - Options
(A) All historians are mathematicians.
(B) No historians are mathematicians.
(C) Some historians are mathematicians.
(D) Some historians are not mathematicians.

## Q16 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Logical Reasoning (Venn, Syllogism, Arguments)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q16

By the logical rule of obversion, any categorical proposition can be transformed into an equivalent proposition by changing its quality and replacing the predicate with its complement.

The given proposition is an universal negative E proposition:<br>
No S is non-P

Applying obversion:

1. Change the quality from negative to affirmative, giving the universal affirmative A form.
2. Replace the predicate term non-mathematician with its complement, which is mathematician.

This yields the equivalent proposition:<br>
All historians are mathematicians.

## Q17
If the proposition ‘Houses are not bricks’ is taken to be False then which of the following propositions can be True ?

(1) All houses are bricks<br>
(2) No house is brick<br>
(3) Some houses are bricks<br>
(4) Some houses are not bricks

Select the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q17 - Options
(A) Statements (2) and (3)
(B) Statements (1) and (4)
(C) Statement (2) only
(D) Statement (3) only

## Q17 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Logical Reasoning (Venn, Syllogism, Arguments)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q17

In classical categorical logic, the proposition Houses are not bricks is an E proposition (No houses are bricks).

According to the Square of Opposition:

- The contradictory of the universal negative E proposition is the particular affirmative I proposition, Some houses are bricks (statement 3).
- Contradictory propositions always have opposite truth values. When E is False, its contradictory I must be True.

Evaluating the options:

- Statement (2) is identical to the given False proposition, so any option containing (2) is invalid.
- In option B, statement (1) and statement (4) are contradictories of each other and cannot both be true simultaneously.
- Therefore, statement (3) is the only proposition guaranteed to be True.

## Q19
‘All republics are grateful’ and ‘Some republics are not grateful’ cannot both be true, and they cannot both be false. This is called as

## Q19 - Options
(A) contraries
(B) contradictories
(C) subaltern
(D) super altern

## Q19 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Logical Reasoning (Venn, Syllogism, Arguments)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q19

In the classical Square of Opposition, a universal affirmative A proposition and a particular negative O proposition share the contradictory relationship.

- **A. contraries** — relates A and E propositions, which cannot both be true simultaneously, but can both be false.
- **B. contradictories** — correct. Defined precisely as two propositions that cannot both be true and cannot both be false at the same time.
- **C. subaltern** — the relationship between a universal proposition and its corresponding particular proposition of the same quality.
- **D. super altern** — denotes the universal form in relation to its particular subaltern.

## Q20

## Q20 - Options
(A) Information – exposure – persuasion – behavioural change.
(B) Persuasion – information – behavioural change – exposure.
(C) Exposure – information – persuasion – behavioural change.
(D) Behavioural change – information – persuasion – exposure.

## Q20 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Communication
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q20

Communication and adoption models trace message impact across distinct cognitive and affective stages.

The standard chronological progression follows:

1. Exposure — the audience first encounters the message through a media channel
2. Information — the audience receives and comprehends the substantive content
3. Persuasion — the audience develops a positive evaluation or attitude toward the proposal
4. Behavioural change — the audience translates conviction into actual practice or adoption

## Q21
Given below are two premises with four conclusions drawn from them. Which of the following conclusions could be validly drawn from the premises ?

Premises:<br>
(i) No paper is pen<br>
(ii) Some paper are handmade

Conclusions:<br>
(a) All paper are handmade<br>
(b) Some handmade are pen<br>
(c) Some handmade are not pen<br>
(d) All handmade are paper

## Q21 - Options
(A) All paper are handmade
(B) Some handmade are pen
(C) Some handmade are not pen
(D) All handmade are paper

## Q21 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Logical Reasoning (Venn, Syllogism, Arguments)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q21

In standard categorical syllogistic logic, combining an E premise and an I premise with a shared middle term yields a valid particular negative O conclusion.

Analyzing the set relations:

- Premise (i) establishes that the class of paper and the class of pen are completely disjoint.
- Premise (ii) asserts that an intersection exists between paper and handmade items.

Those handmade items that fall within the paper class cannot be pens because no paper is a pen. Therefore, the conclusion that some handmade are not pen is validly deduced.

## Q22

**Answer:** D

**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q22

To divide a quantity according to a given ratio, first sum the component ratio parts.

Sum of parts:<br>
3 + 4 + 5 + 7 = 19

Value of one part:<br>
152 / 19 = 8

Calculating the smallest part, corresponding to ratio 3:<br>
3 × 8 = 24

## Q27
For all integers y &gt; 1, ⟨y⟩ = 2y + (2y − 1) + (2y − 2) + ··· + 1. What is the value of ⟨3⟩ × ⟨2⟩ ? Where × is a multiplication operator?

## Q27 - Options
(A) 116
(B) 210
(C) 263
(D) 478

## Q27 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Mathematical Aptitude (Arithmetic)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q27

The defined operator represents the sum of the first 2y positive integers, given by the formula n(n + 1) / 2 where n = 2y.

Calculating ⟨3⟩ where y = 3 and n = 6:<br>
6 + 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 21

Calculating ⟨2⟩ where y = 2 and n = 4:<br>
4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10

Multiplying the two evaluated terms:<br>
21 × 10 = 210

## Q28
In a new budget, the price of petrol rose by 25 %. By how much percent must a person reduce his consumption so that his expenditure on it does not increase ?

## Q28 - Options
(A) 10 %
(B) 15 %
(C) 20 %
(D) 25 %

## Q28 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Mathematical Aptitude (Arithmetic)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q28

When the price of a commodity increases by r percent, the percentage reduction in consumption required to keep expenditure constant is given by [r / (100 + r)] × 100.

Substituting r = 25 into the formula:<br>
[25 / (100 + 25)] × 100<br>
= [25 / 125] × 100<br>
= (1 / 5) × 100<br>
= 20 %

## Q29

## Q29 - Options
(A) A transactional model

(C) A horizontal model
(D) A linear model

## Q29 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Communication
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q29

In an active group discussion, communicators simultaneously send and receive verbal and non-verbal cues, collaboratively co-creating shared meaning in a shared social environment.

- **A. A transactional model** — correct. Captures continuous, simultaneous, reciprocal message exchange where participants are both senders and receivers.
- **B. An interaction model** — views communication as an alternating, turn-based circular exchange with delayed feedback rather than simultaneous co-presence.
- **C. A horizontal model** — describes lateral communication among organizational peers on the same administrative hierarchy level.
- **D. A linear model** — represents unidirectional, one-way communication from a sender to a passive receiver with no feedback mechanism.

## Q30
A sum of money doubles at compound interest in 6 years. In how many years will it become 16 times?

## Q30 - Options
(A) 16 years
(B) 24 years
(C) 48 years
(D) 96 years

## Q30 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Mathematical Aptitude (Arithmetic)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q30

Under compound interest, an investment grows exponentially by the same compounding multiple across equal time intervals.

If the principal doubles in 6 years:<br>
2^1 times in 6 years

To become 16 times the original principal, express 16 as a power of 2:<br>
16 = 2^4

Multiplying the exponent by the doubling interval:<br>
4 × 6 = 24 years

## Q44
Assertion (A): Mathemoglobinemia is a condition in which blood is not able to carry and deliver enough oxygen to the body.<br>
Reason (R): Consuming drinking water with high nitrate levels may cause methemoglobinemia

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

## Q44 - Options
(A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(C) (A) is true but (R) is false
(D) (A) is false but (R) is true.

## Q44 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Environment (Pollution, Climate, Resources, Hazards)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q44

Methemoglobinemia (commonly known as blue baby syndrome in infants) is a blood disorder characterized by elevated levels of methemoglobin.

Evaluating the statements:

- Assertion (A) is true because methemoglobin carries iron in the ferric (Fe3+) state rather than the normal ferrous (Fe2+) state, preventing it from binding oxygen and releasing it to bodily tissues.
- Reason (R) is true because drinking groundwater contaminated with agricultural nitrates introduces compounds that are converted into nitrites in the digestive tract, oxidizing hemoglobin into methemoglobin.

Because consuming nitrate-rich drinking water directly induces the formation of methemoglobin and triggers the oxygen-deprivation syndrome, Reason (R) provides the recognized causal explanation for Assertion (A).

Standard optical storage formats differ significantly in track density, laser wavelength, and data capacity.

Standard data capacities:

- DVD-ROM: 4.7 GB (single-layer) to 8.5 GB (dual-layer) using a red laser (650 nm)
- Blu-ray Disc: 25 GB (single-layer) to 50 GB (dual-layer) using a blue-violet laser (405 nm)

Arranging from lowest to highest storage capacity gives:<br>
CD-ROM &lt; DVD-ROM &lt; Blu-ray

## Q48
The Education Commission of India that first took serious note of the problem of Brain Drain was

## Q48 - Options
(A) The Education Commission of India
(B) The University Education Commission
(C) The Calcutta University Commission
(D) The Sargeant Commission

## Q48 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q48

The Education Commission of India (1964–66), headed by D. S. Kothari, was the first official statutory commission in India to formally investigate and sound the alarm on the loss of highly trained scientific talent abroad.

In its comprehensive report, the Commission devoted specific attention to the emigration of doctors, scientists, engineers, and scholars to developed nations, which it termed Brain Drain, urging the government to establish research infrastructure and competitive conditions to retain Indian intellectuals.

- **A. The Education Commission of India** — correct. The official title of the Kothari Commission (1964–66).
- **B. The University Education Commission** — headed by Dr. S. Radhakrishnan (1948–49), focused on foundational university development.
- **C. The Calcutta University Commission** — the Sadler Commission (1917–19), examined university and secondary schooling in Bengal during colonial rule.
- **D. The Sargeant Commission** — the 1944 pre-independence scheme for post-war educational reconstruction.

## Q49
Assertion (A): Higher concentration of ozone in the lower troposphere is desirable<br>
Reason (R): Ozone present in the atmosphere protects the living organisms on the surface of earth from the harmful ultra-violet radiation of the sun.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

## Q49 - Options
(A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(C) (A) is true but (R) is false
(D) (A) is false but (R) is true

## Q49 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Environment (Pollution, Climate, Resources, Hazards)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q49

Ozone acts as either a vital protective shield or a hazardous toxic pollutant depending on the atmospheric layer in which it resides.

Evaluating the statements:

- Assertion (A) is False because ground-level tropospheric ozone is a harmful secondary air pollutant and key constituent of photochemical smog, damaging respiratory tissue, lungs, and vegetation.
- Reason (R) is True because stratospheric ozone (located between 15 and 35 km above the earth) absorbs harmful solar ultraviolet (UV-B) radiation, protecting life on Earth from cellular damage.

Because tropospheric ozone is dangerous rather than desirable, (A) is false while (R) is true.

## Q50
Select the true statement about an Operation System (OS)?

## Q50 - Options
(A) An OS controls peripherals, allocates memory and organises data into field and records
(B) An OS provides protection against viruses and controals peripherals
(C) An OS controal peripheral, and allocates memory and processor time
(D) An OS controls the processor and peripherals and allows the user the connect to the Internet.

## Q50 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** ICT (Computers, Internet, Terminology)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q50

An Operating System is foundational system software responsible for managing computer hardware resources and scheduling system activities.

The core resource management tasks of an operating system are:

- Device management — controlling peripheral devices through drivers and interrupts
- Memory management — allocating and deallocating primary RAM to active processes
- Processor management — scheduling CPU execution time across competing threads
- **A. An OS controls peripherals, allocates memory and organises data into field and records** — organising data into fields and records is the specific domain of Database Management Systems (DBMS).
- **B. An OS provides protection against viruses and controals peripherals** — antivirus protection is specialized utility security software rather than the core definition of an operating system.
- **C. An OS controal peripheral, and allocates memory and processor time** — correct. Accurately describes fundamental OS hardware resource allocation (peripherals, memory, and processor time).
- **D. An OS controls the processor and peripherals and allows the user the connect to the Internet.** — internet connectivity requires external networking protocols, modems, and network software rather than defining the OS role.
